pick.name: Auto mode + allow/deny rules on Windows; WSL2 /sandbox for untrusted repos
pick.what: Classifier-gated autonomy natively; bubblewrap sandbox only in WSL2
pick.why: Native Windows has no Bash sandbox, so bypass mode runs every command unisolated, which matters most on a company-managed laptop
pick.free_limits: All plans; native Windows needs Claude Code v2.1.233+; auto is the default starting mode from v2.1.283
pick.install: ~/.claude/settings.json: "defaultMode": "auto" (user settings only) + deny rules via /permissions; in WSL: sudo apt-get install bubblewrap socat, then /sandbox

decision: Swap bypass for auto mode with explicit deny rules; use the WSL2 sandbox or a dev container for unknown repos and healthcare client code.

verify.note: Auto mode exists as described: a separate classifier reviews actions; available on ALL plans (not a Max feature), needs v2.1.233+ on native Windows, and is the built-in default mode from v2.1.283. Persist it with defaultMode 'auto' in ~/.claude/settings.json (project-level 'auto' does not take effect). Sandbox doc confirms: native Windows runs commands unsandboxed; WSL2 needs bubblewrap + socat.
